Why was the errata put on Elder Impersonation?

The failed blocker is not untapped, but rather "not tapped" - if the
blocker was tapped originally, he will remain tapped
(errata). [RTR 19960708]

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In article <8r2tdi$f4a$1...@nnrp1.deja.com>, X_Ze...@email.msn.com writes

>The failed blocker is not untapped, but rather "not tapped" - if the
>blocker was tapped originally, he will remain tapped
> (errata). [RTR 19960708]

A vampire using Wake should not be untapped.

The original intent of the card was to leave the blocking vampire in
their original state. "Untapped" does that in all circumstances, except
a vampire who was originally tapped and used Wake, or whatever. "Not
tapped" does it in all circumstances.

No. Elder Impersonation doesn't cancel a tapping effect - it just
reminds the reader that, as the block was unsuccessful, the would-be
blocker is not tapped for successfully blocking.
